content.title: Route Collapse | Safe Space Erosion
content.summary: The subject moves exclusively toward a fixed endpoint, with the traversed route disappearing sequentially. The connection is finally severed only after the subject completely crosses the threshold.

quick_start.input_format: Carrier + Fixed Direction and Endpoint + Traversed Route Disappears Segment by Segment + Current Segment Experiences One Instance of Instability + Final Disconnection Occurs Only After Fully Crossing the Threshold
quick_start.recommended_input: The sampling vehicle in the transparent greenhouse pipeline continuously travels toward the safety cabin, with each traversed section collapsing sequentially; the current section sways only once, and the final connection is severed only after the vehicle fully enters the safety cabin.
required_anchors: The rear route can only decrease, not increase.
The current segment can recover from instability at most once.
The final connection is severed only after the subject has completely crossed the threshold.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: The subject only moves towards a fixed end point, and the route it has taken disappears monotonically, and the connection is finally disconnected after it completely crosses the threshold.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Lock one subject to a single screen-direction destination, then remove traversed route segments monotonically from behind while introducing one instability under the current segment. Alternate local control proof with wide remaining-route proof, and end with the subject fully crossing a safety threshold one beat before the final connection fails.

invariants.rule: Establish one visible destination and one travel direction.
Remove only already-traversed safe space from behind.
invariants.purpose: Prevents arbitrary danger and blocks retreat.
invariants.ablation_failure: Random forward gaps can make survival impossible rather than tense.

invariants.rule: Add one recoverable instability under the current segment.
invariants.purpose: Tests control without replacing route logic.
invariants.ablation_failure: Too many local hazards obscure the monotonic collapse.

invariants.rule: Alternate close control with wide remaining-route evidence.
invariants.purpose: Proves both agency and structural countdown.
invariants.ablation_failure: Only close shots hide how much route remains.

invariants.rule: Cross the full threshold before the last connection fails.
invariants.ablation_failure: Cutting away before full crossing leaves the outcome uncertain.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original subject or system whose identity remains stable.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One visible variable that changes in countable causal stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained behavior rule that makes the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: A coherent information order that does not copy source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: One clean physical or graphic consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: A new hierarchy of diegetic cues supporting state changes.

anti_copy_exclusions: dark SUV on a suspension bridge
sliding abandoned cars and snapping cables
the source bridge-deck collapse and far-shore anchorage
